models_evaluated: ML model predicting massive intraoperative blood loss (>2,500 mL) in spinal metastasis surgery

links.outcome: Distributional shift between development and validation cohorts in predictive variables
links.effect: Poor performance attributed partly to distributional shift, as the validation cohort had key differences in predictive variables used by the model.
links.quote: This poor performance might be attributed to overfitting and sampling bias as the development cohort had an insufficient sample size, and distributional shift as our cohort had key differences in predictive variables used by the model.

links.outcome: Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility on external cohorts versus developer results
links.effect: Model overestimated risk; Brier 0.278, AUC 0.631 (95%CI 0.583-0.680), calibration slope 0.283, net harm on decision curve analysis from 20% threshold.
links.quote: Using the most favorable quantification method, the predictive model overestimated risk in our total validation cohort and scored poorly on overall fit (Brier score: 0.278), discrimination (AUC: 0.631 [95%CI: 0.583, 0.680]), calibration, (intercept: -2.082, [95%CI: -2.285, -1.879]), slope: 0.283 [95%CI: 0.173, 0.393]), and clinical utility, with net harm observed in decision curve analysis from 20%.

links.outcome: Performance across sites/regions (North American and European cohorts separately)
links.effect: Similar poor performance observed in North American (n=539) and European (n=341) cohorts analyzed separately and in the subanalysis (n=676).
links.quote: Similar poor performance results were observed in the subanalysis excluding the additional included patients (n=676) and when analyzing the North American (n=539) and European (n=341) cohorts separately.

links.outcome: Overestimated performance from insufficient sample size, overfitting, and lack of external validation
links.effect: Poor external performance attributed to overfitting and sampling bias from an insufficient development sample size.
links.quote: These findings emphasize the importance of extensive validation in different geographical areas and addressing biases and pitfalls of ML model development before clinical implementation, as untested models may do more harm than good.

screen.reason: The study conducts an independent multi-institutional external validation of an existing machine learning prediction model across different continents (North America and Europe) to evaluate generalization performance and transportability before clinical implementation.
